keyIdea:
A **compound measure** combines two units.
$$\text{density} = \frac{\text{mass}}{\text{volume}} \qquad \text{pressure} = \frac{\text{force}}{\text{area}} \qquad \text{flow rate} = \frac{\text{volume}}{\text{time}}$$
Units: g/cm³ or kg/m³; N/m² (pascals, Pa) or N/cm²; litres per minute.

Rearrange as needed: mass $=$ density $\times$ volume, volume $=$ mass $\div$ density, force $=$ pressure $\times$ area.

**Units must match**: with density in g/cm³, use mass in g and volume in cm³. Remember $1\text{ m}^2 = 10\,000\text{ cm}^2$ and $1\text{ m}^3 = 1\,000\,000\text{ cm}^3$.

**Mixtures/alloys**: total mass $\div$ total volume. Never average the densities.

For the same force, a larger area gives a smaller pressure.

**Density in modelling:** the same idea measures how crowded anything is, e.g. population density $= \frac{\text{people}}{\text{area}}$ (people per $\text{km}^2$), or trees per hectare; compare places with it, or multiply by an area to estimate a total.
